mainTopic: Combining half-amounts for הוצאה on שבת (ink, half-גרוגרות, separate domains), and the משנה's שיעורים for כחול, wax, glue, tar, חרסית and bran.
overview: This amud continues the discussion of the minimum amounts (שיעורים) that make someone liable for הוצאה on שבת. A תוספתא sets the ink amount at two letters. רבא asks whether ink in different forms combines, and that question stays unresolved (תיקו). רבא then rules on writing while walking and on carrying ink one letter at a time. He also rules on two half-גרוגרות carried separately, which brings in the rules of 'within three טפחים' and the difference between throwing (זורק) and passing by hand (מעביר). A ברייתא teaches that two halves combine only within one העלם. רבי יוסי adds that both halves must also reach one רשות, and רבה, אביי and רבא disagree about what kind of divider makes two domains. The גמרא then explains several items from the משנה's list: eye paint (כחול), wax, glue, tar and sulfur, crushed earthenware, and bran. Each one is measured by a real, everyday use.

steps.title: Ink in three forms: two letters each
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the שיעור for carrying ink is enough for two letters, whether the ink is dried, in a quill, or in an inkwell.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: enough for two letters in dried ink, two letters in the quill, and two letters in the inkwell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא (תוספתא) that sets the amount of ink that makes you liable. The amount is the same in every form the ink takes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ink can be carried as dried ink, wet ink on a pen, or ink in a well. Each form has one standard: enough ink to write two letters. This sets up רבא's question about mixing the forms.

phrases.english: It was taught: two letters in dried ink,
two letters in the quill,
two letters in the inkwell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the ink שיעור for הוצאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שיעור for carrying ink is enough to write two letters, in any of its three forms.

steps.title: Do different forms of ink combine?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether one letter's worth in each of the three forms adds up to make him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: one letter's worth in dried ink, one letter's worth in the quill, one letter's worth in the inkwell — what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a real question (בעיא). Someone carried a little ink in each form. Does it add up to the שיעור?
steps.deeperAnalysis: No single form reaches the two-letter amount. The question is whether ink in different states counts as one kind of item, so the amounts combine, or as separate items that cannot join.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (introduces a real halachic question)

phrases.english: Rava asked:
one letter in dried ink,
one letter in the quill,
one letter in the inkwell — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא by asking about a mixed case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether small amounts of ink in different forms join to make the two-letter שיעור.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question is left open: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds no answer, so it leaves רבא's question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the question 'stands' without a decision. The case of mixed ink forms stays an open doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand — the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 2 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether different forms of ink combine stays an unresolved doubt.

steps.title: Writing while walking counts as setting down
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that someone who carries out ink for two letters and writes them while walking is liable, because the writing counts as the הנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he carried out enough ink for two letters and wrote them while walking, he is liable. Writing them is the same as setting them down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule. Normally הוצאה requires picking up (עקירה) and setting down (הנחה), but here the writing itself serves as the setting down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person never stopped or put the ink down on the ground. Still, once the ink is written onto a surface in the new domain, the ink has come to rest there. So the carrying is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting down — the final stage of הוצאה

phrases.english: Rava said: If he carried out two letters' worth of ink
and wrote them while he was walking — he is liable,
their writing is their setting down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the size of the שיעור to how the carrying is completed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Writing the ink in the new domain counts as its הנחה, so he is liable even while walking.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that הנחה does not have to mean physically putting the item on the ground. Any way the item comes to rest can count.

steps.title: One letter at a time is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that carrying out ink for one letter, writing it, and then doing the same again is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If he carried out ink for one letter and wrote it, and then carried out ink for one more letter and wrote it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second rule. Two separate trips of one letter's worth each do not add up to liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the end two letters were written, which matches the שיעור. But each trip carried only half the amount, and he is exempt. The reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: And he went back (and did it again)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הוֹצִיא אוֹת אַחַת וּכְתָבָהּ,
phrases.english: And Rava said: If he carried out one letter and wrote it,

phrases.aramaic: וְחָזַר וְהוֹצִיא אוֹת אַחַת וּכְתָבָהּ — פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: and then carried out one letter and wrote it — he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of רבא about ink, contrasting with step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two separate one-letter trips do not combine; he is exempt.

steps.title: Why is he exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבא's exemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why he is exempt. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two letters were written in the end, so one could think the amounts should combine. The גמרא wants to know what stops them from joining.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the logic of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the two one-letter trips do not combine to the שיעור.

steps.title: The first ink dried before the second came out
steps.stepSummary: By the time he carried out the second amount, the first had dried and no longer held a full letter's worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the time he carried out the last one, the amount of the first one was already lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains: when the second ink was carried out, the first ink had shrunk. There was never a full two-letter amount at one time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wet ink dries over time and loses some of its amount. So when the second letter's worth arrived, the first was already less than one letter. The total never reached the שיעור together.

phrases.english: At the time that he carried out the last one,
the amount of the first one was lacking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first ink dried and shrank, so the two amounts never existed together as a full שיעור.
steps.whatToRemember: Two half-amounts join only if the full שיעור exists together at one moment. Ink that dried in between breaks the combination.

steps.title: Two half-figs carried separately
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules about carrying half a גרוגרת, setting it down, then carrying another half: the first half is treated as gone, and he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If he carried out half a dried fig and set it down, and then carried out another half and set it down, the first one is treated as if a dog snatched it or it burned, and he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא moves to food, where the שיעור is a גרוגרת (dried fig). He rules that two separate half-figs make him exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half is treated as if it no longer exists, as if a dog took it or it burned up. So the second half has nothing to join with. The wording is puzzling, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Dried fig — the standard food שיעור for הוצאה

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הוֹצִיא חֲצִי גְרוֹגֶרֶת אַחַת וְהִנִּיחָה,
phrases.english: And Rava said: If he carried out half of a dried fig and set it down,

phrases.aramaic: וְחָזַר וְהוֹצִיא חֲצִי גְרוֹגֶרֶת אַחַת וְהִנִּיחָה —
phrases.english: and then carried out another half of a dried fig and set it down —
the first becomes as if a dog snatched it
or as if it was burned, and he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the idea of combining half-amounts to food instead of ink.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two half-figs carried separately: the first is treated as gone, and he is exempt.

steps.title: But both halves are resting there together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: both halves are now lying in the new domain, so a full fig was set down.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Isn't it resting there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling. If both halves are lying there together, a full גרוגרת is in the new domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing actually happened to the first half. It is still lying there when the second half lands. So it seems a full שיעור was set down, and he should be liable.

phrases.english: And why? Isn't it resting there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that two half-figs set down separately are exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both halves are lying together in the new domain, so a full גרוגרת has been set down.

steps.title: The first half was picked up before the second landed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets רבא: he meant a case where the first half was lifted up before the second half was set down.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: if he first lifted the first half before setting down the second, the first is treated as if snatched or burned, and he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by explaining the case more precisely. The two halves were never lying there at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first half was picked up before the second was set down, the two halves never rested together. That is why the first is treated as if it were gone. If both halves did lie there together, he would be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (reinterprets the statement)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבא's ruling as covering any two half-figs carried separately. After this answer it applies only when the first half was removed before the second arrived.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
and if he first lifted up the first one
before setting down the second —
the first becomes as if it was snatched
or as if it was burned, and he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא was talking about two halves that both lay there together.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא was talking about a case where the first half was lifted before the second was set down, so they never rested together.
steps.whatToRemember: Half-figs join only if they rest together at the same time. If they never do, each half is a separate act below the שיעור.

steps.title: Passing the second half over the first makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if he set down one half and then carried a second half over it, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If he carried out half a dried fig and set it down, and then carried out another half and passed it over the first, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another case. Here the second half only passed over the first and was never set down, yet he is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, because a full הוצאה normally needs a הנחה. The second half never rested, yet רבא says the two halves combine. The גמרא will question this next.

keyTerms.meaning: And he passed it (carried it across)
By way of over it (over the first half)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הוֹצִיא חֲצִי גְרוֹגֶרֶת וְהִנִּיחָהּ,
phrases.english: And Rava said: If he carried out half a dried fig and set it down,
and then carried out another half of a dried fig
and passed it over it — he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite case to step 10: the halves come close together instead of being apart.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Passing the second half over the first half that is resting makes him liable.

steps.title: But the second half never came to rest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the second half was only passed over and never set down, so why is he liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? It did not come to rest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא. Without a הנחה of the second half, how can there be liability?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for הוצאה requires the item to come to rest. The second half was only moving through the air. So the full amount was never set down together.

keyTerms.meaning: But it did not come to rest!

phrases.english: And why? It did not come to rest!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that passing the second half over the first makes him liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second half never came to rest, and הוצאה requires הנחה.

steps.title: He passed it within three טפחים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he passed the second half within three טפחים of the first, so it counts as resting with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where he passed it within three handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second half passed very close to the first, within three טפחים. Something that close is treated as touching or resting there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that things less than three טפחים apart are treated as joined (לבוד). So the second half is treated as resting on top of the first, and together they make a full גרוגרת.

keyTerms.meaning: For example / it is a case where

phrases.english: For example, where he passed it within three handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second half just flew past without resting at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It passed within three טפחים of the first half, so it counts as resting on it.

steps.title: רבא himself said within three still needs resting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges with רבא's own statement that, according to the רבנן, an item within three טפחים must still rest on something.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא say: within three handbreadths, according to the רבנן, it needs to rest on top of something!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction from another statement of רבא. There he said being within three טפחים is not enough, and the item must actually rest on something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, being close to the ground (within three טפחים) does not count as resting by itself. The item needs to land on some surface. That seems to undo the answer in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say: within three handbreadths, according to the Rabbis,
it needs to rest on top of something!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13 with a contradiction from רבא himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that passing within three טפחים counts as resting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא himself ruled that according to the רבנן, an item within three טפחים must actually rest on something to count as placed.

steps.title: Throwing versus passing by hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule requiring actual resting is about throwing, while our case is about passing an item by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here it is about one who throws, and here it is about one who passes it in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by separating two cases. A thrown item must land, but an item held in the hand counts as resting once it is within three טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When something is thrown, the thrower has no control over it, so it must actually land. When a person carries an item in his hand, he can set it down whenever he wants. So being within three טפחים is treated as resting, and both of רבא's statements stand.

keyTerms.meaning: One who passes an item in his hand

steps.whatToRemember: Within three טפחים: a thrown item must actually land (according to the רבנן). An item passed by hand counts as resting there, so two half-figs can combine.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same distance rule can work differently depending on how the item moves: throwing versus carrying by hand.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here it is about one who throws, here about one who passes it by hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Within three טפחים always requires actual resting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Actual resting is required only for a thrown item. An item passed by hand counts as resting within three טפחים.

steps.title: Two half-figs carried out in one lapse or in two lapses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that two half-גרוגרות carried out combine to make him חייב only if both were done in one העלם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If someone carried out half a dried fig and then carried out another half, he is liable if it was all in one lapse of awareness. If it was in two lapses, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about whether two small acts of carrying can add up to one full שיעור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שיעור for carrying food is a full גרוגרת, and each act here was only half. If he never remembered in between (one העלם), the two halves join together and he brings a חטאת. If he remembered in between, the knowing breaks them apart, so neither half reaches a full שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: A dried fig, the standard measure for carrying food
One lapse of awareness (he forgot the whole time)
Two lapses of awareness, with a remembering in between

steps.confusionAlert: Being פטור here does not mean the carrying was allowed. It only means he does not bring a קרבן חטאת, because no single act reached the full שיעור.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If one carried out half a dried fig
and then again carried out half a dried fig,
in one lapse of awareness, he is liable;
in two lapses of awareness, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: Remembering in between separates the two acts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about combining half-measures. This follows the earlier discussion of half-items and resting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two halves combine to make him חייב only within one העלם.

steps.title: רבי יוסי requires both halves to reach one domain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי adds a condition: the halves combine only if both were carried into the same רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: In one lapse of awareness, into one domain, he is liable. Into two domains, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds another condition to the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, one העלם is not enough. The two halves must also end up in the same רשות so they can be seen as one act. If they landed in two separate areas of רשות הרבים, they do not combine.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
in one lapse of awareness, to one domain, he is liable;
to two domains, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second condition to the תנא קמא's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halves combine only if both are carried into the same רשות.

steps.title: רבה: only a Torah-level divider makes two domains
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that רבי יוסי's 'two domains' means areas separated by a place where carrying brings a חטאת. A כרמלית in between does not separate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This is only when there is a place between them where carrying makes one liable for a sin-offering. But if a כרמלית is between them, they are not separate.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defines what counts as 'two domains' in רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two areas of רשות הרבים are separate only if a רשות היחיד lies between them, because carrying across it is forbidden by the Torah. A כרמלית is forbidden only מדרבנן, so on the Torah level the two areas still count as one. In that case, the halves combine and he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Liability to bring a sin-offering (a Torah-level violation)
An in-between area, forbidden for carrying only by Rabbinic law

phrases.english: Rabba said:
That is, when there is sin-offering liability between them.
But a karmelit, no.
phrases.notes: A כרמלית in between does not make them separate domains.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: וְהוּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ חִיּוּב חַטָּאת בֵּינֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term 'two domains' in רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a Torah-level divider, such as a רשות היחיד, separates the two areas. A כרמלית does not.

steps.title: אביי: even a כרמלית separates, but not a beam
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that even a כרמלית in between makes two domains. A פיסלא (beam) does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even a כרמלית separates them. But a large beam does not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי disagrees with רבה and widens what counts as a divider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, a כרמלית is enough to split the area into two רשויות, so the halves do not combine. But a mere beam lying in the area is not a real separate domain, so it does not divide.

keyTerms.meaning: A large beam or board placed in the area

phrases.english: Abaye said: Even a karmelit.
But a large beam, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A competing definition of what separates two domains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כרמלית separates domains. A פיסלא does not.

steps.title: רבא: even a beam separates
steps.stepSummary: רבא goes furthest and says that even a פיסלא splits the area into two domains.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Even a large beam separates them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third, even broader view of what makes two domains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, even a beam dividing the area is enough to make two separate רשויות. So the halves do not combine, and he is פטור according to רבי יוסי.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה (רבה) and רבא (רבא) are two different אמוראים with opposite views here. Watch the spelling.

phrases.english: And Rava said: Even a large beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens אביי's view to include even a beam.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a פיסלא separates two domains.

steps.title: רבא is consistent with his rule about divorce documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא's view fits his general rule that רשות for שבת works like רשות for גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא follows his own reasoning, as רבא said: A domain for שבת is like a domain for divorce documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא's view here matches another rule he taught elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In גיטין, a beam can divide a space into separate domains. רבא holds that 'domain' means the same thing for שבת. That is why he says a פיסלא separates here too.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (is consistent)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: only a Torah-level divider separates. אביי: even a כרמלית separates, but not a beam. רבא: even a beam separates, just like in גיטין.

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own reasoning,
for Rava said:
The domain of Shabbat is like the domain of divorce documents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's view by linking it to his rule elsewhere.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that a פיסלא separates domains
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's rule that רשות for שבת is the same as רשות for גיטין

steps.title: The משנה's measure for eye paint
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the שיעור for carrying כחול is enough to paint one eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: eye paint, enough to paint one eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes a new line. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the topic changes to the שיעורים of the משנה. The words 'one eye' will be challenged right away.

phrases.english: Eye paint: enough to paint one eye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שיעור for carrying כחול is enough for one eye.

steps.title: But nobody paints only one eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the measure is one eye, since women do not paint only one eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: One eye? But women do not paint just one eye!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שיעור is based on a normal, useful amount. If no one ever paints just one eye, then one eye's worth seems too small to count as important.

keyTerms.meaning: But they do not paint (that way)

phrases.english: One eye? But they do not paint one eye!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה's measure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's שיעור of one eye
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שיעור must match normal use, and normally both eyes are painted.

steps.title: Modest women paint only one eye
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that צנועות, who cover their faces, paint only the one eye that shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Because modest women paint only one eye.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question by showing that some women really do paint only one eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Modest women wear a veil that leaves only one eye showing, so they paint just that eye. Since painting one eye is a real practice, one eye's worth is a meaningful amount.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Because modest women paint one eye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a real practice exists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No one paints only one eye, so the measure makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Modest, veiled women paint one eye, so one eye is a normal amount.

steps.title: A ברייתא says decoration needs two eyes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who says that for decoration the measure is two eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: For eye paint, if it is for healing, the measure is enough for one eye. If it is for decoration, the measure is for two eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only healing uses one eye in this ברייתא. Decoration always needs two eyes. That goes against רב הונא, who said that even for beauty, modest women paint only one eye.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Eye paint: if for healing,
enough to paint one eye;
if for decoration, for two eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that decoration can be one eye
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says one eye applies only to healing. Decoration requires two eyes.

steps.title: The ברייתא refers to village women
steps.stepSummary: הילל בריה דרבי שמואל בר נחמני explains that the ברייתא speaks about village women, who do not veil and so paint both eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: הילל, son of רבי שמואל בר נחמני, explained it: That ברייתא was taught about village women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by limiting the ברייתא to a different group of women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Village women do not cover their faces, so for beauty they paint both eyes. The ברייתא's two-eye measure is about them. רב הונא's one-eye measure is about veiled women in the cities, so the two sources do not argue.
steps.whatToRemember: The one-eye measure fits modest, veiled women. The two-eye measure in the ברייתא is about village women, who do not veil.

phrases.english: Hillel explained it,
son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani:
When that was taught, it was about village women.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ הִילֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says decoration always means two eyes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only village women always paint two eyes. Veiled city women paint one.

steps.title: The משנה's measure for wax
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the שיעור for carrying שעוה is enough to seal a small hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: wax, enough to put over a small hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the clarification in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה measures wax by its common use, which is plugging a small hole. But it does not say what kind of small hole.

phrases.aramaic: (שַׁעֲוָה כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן עַל פִּי נֶקֶב קָטָן.
phrases.english: Wax: enough to place over the opening of a small hole.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁעֲוָה כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן עַל פִּי נֶקֶב קָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שיעור for carrying שעוה is enough to seal a small hole.

steps.title: A small hole of a wine vessel
steps.stepSummary: A תנא clarifies that the 'small hole' is the small hole of a wine vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: Enough to place over a small hole of a wine vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains which small hole the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole for pouring wine is smaller than holes used for thicker liquids. So the שיעור for wax is set by this very small hole, which makes it a small amount.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא taught (introduces a ברייתא or תוספתא)

phrases.english: A tanna taught:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן עַל פִּי נֶקֶב קָטָן שֶׁל יַיִן.)
phrases.english: enough to place over the opening of a small hole of wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן עַל פִּי נֶקֶב קָטָן שֶׁל יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the משנה's term 'small hole'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'small hole' means the small hole of a wine vessel.

steps.title: The משנה's measure for glue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the שיעור for carrying out דבק is enough to put on the top of a שפשף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Glue: enough to put on the top of the board.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item from the משנה, which is glue. This sets up the תנא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only 'the top of the שפשף' and does not say which board it means. That leaves room for the clarification that comes next.

phrases.english: Glue: enough to put
on the top of the board.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from wax to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying glue is חייב when there is enough to coat the top of a שפשף.

steps.title: The board is the one on a hunter's rod
steps.stepSummary: A תנא explains that the שפשף is the board on top of a hunter's rod.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: enough to put on the top of the board that is at the top of the hunters' rod.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא tells us which board the משנה means. It is the small board hunters fixed on top of a pole and smeared with glue to catch birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the measure is clear. It is the amount of glue a hunter actually uses for a real job, which is trapping birds. As with the other items on this list, the שיעור is tied to a useful, everyday purpose.

phrases.english: It was taught: enough to put on the top of the board
that is at the top of the hunters' rod.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן בְּרֹאשׁ שַׁפְשָׁף שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ קָנֶה שֶׁל צַיָּידִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which שפשף the משנה is talking about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שפשף is the bird-trapping board at the top of a hunter's rod.

steps.title: The משנה's measure for tar and sulfur
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's measure for זפת וגפרית: enough to make a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tar and sulfur: enough to make a hole, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, which is tar and sulfur. This sets up the תנא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כו' means the משנה's wording continues, and the גמרא quotes only the start. Tar and sulfur were used to seal openings in jars.

phrases.english: Tar and sulfur:
enough to make, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying tar and sulfur is חייב at the amount needed for the job of making a hole.

steps.title: It means making a small hole
steps.stepSummary: A תנא explains that the measure is enough to make a small hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: enough to make a small hole.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא makes the משנה's measure exact. It is enough tar or sulfur to shrink a big opening down to a small hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this, we would not know how large the 'hole' is. The ברייתא sets the amount as what it takes to narrow a large opening into a small one.

phrases.english: It was taught: enough to make a small hole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה's measure for tar and sulfur.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שיעור is enough to turn a large opening into a small hole.

steps.title: The משנה's measure for crushed earthenware
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the שיעור for חרסית is enough to make the opening of a כור. The rest of the משנה, cut off by כו', is רבי יהודה's view that it is enough to make a פיטפוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Crushed earthenware: enough to make the opening of a crucible, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about crushed earthenware. This sets up a question about רבי יהודה's view in the part of the משנה that is cut off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say the measure is enough to form the opening of a goldsmith's crucible where the bellows goes in. רבי יהודה, in the part hidden by כו', says it is enough to make a פיטפוט, a small stand for the crucible. A whole stand sounds like more material than an opening.

keyTerms.meaning: Crushed earthenware, used as a kind of plaster
The opening of a crucible or furnace

phrases.english: Crushed earthenware: enough to make
the opening of a crucible, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: enough to make a crucible's opening. רבי יהודה: enough to make a פיטפוט.

steps.title: Why would רבי יהודה's measure be larger here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does this mean רבי יהודה's שיעור is bigger? Elsewhere his שיעור is smaller than the רבנן's, as in his measure of a child's shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that רבי יהודה's measure is larger? But we hold that the רבנן's measure is larger, as we learned: רבי יהודה says, enough to take from it the measure of a shoe for a child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. Here רבי יהודה seems to require more than the רבנן, but in another משנה he requires less.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole stand (פיטפוט) sounds bigger than a crucible's opening, so רבי יהודה's measure looks larger. But we know a pattern: in this set of שיעורים, the רבנן's measure is the larger one. Proof is another משנה where רבי יהודה gives a tiny measure, just enough to measure a child's shoe. The גמרא expects רבי יהודה to stay consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say?' It draws out a troubling implication
The measurement for a child's shoe

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'larger measure' means a larger amount needed before you are חייב, which makes that view more lenient. The question is not about who is stricter. It is about whether רבי יהודה is consistent about whose measure is bigger.

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Yehuda's measure is larger?
But we have established
that the Rabbis' measure is larger,
as we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Yehuda says:
enough to take from it
the measure of a shoe for a child.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְפִישׁ? הָא קַיְימָא לַן דְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְרַבָּנַן נְפִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה just quoted by comparing it with another משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's measure for חרסית (a פיטפוט)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פיטפוט seems bigger than פי כור, which goes against the known pattern that רבי יהודה's measures are smaller than the רבנן's (the child's shoe).

steps.title: רבי יהודה means plastering a small stove's stand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: read רבי יהודה as meaning only enough to plaster the stand of a small stove, which is a tiny amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: enough to plaster the stand of a small stove.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading רבי יהודה differently. He does not mean building a whole stand. He means only patching or plastering the small stand of a little stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'making a פיטפוט' is read as just smearing plaster on a small stand, רבי יהודה's amount becomes very small. That is smaller than the רבנן's crucible opening. Now רבי יהודה fits his usual pattern of having the smaller measure.
steps.whatToRemember: In this list of שיעורים, רבי יהודה always holds the smaller measure. So his 'פיטפוט' means only plastering a small stove's stand, not building one.

phrases.english: Say: enough to plaster
the stand of a small stove.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: כְּדֵי לָסוּד פִּיטְפּוּט כִּירָה קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reinterpreting רבי יהודה's measure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה meant making an entire stand, which is a large amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: He means only plastering a small stove's stand, which is a tiny amount and smaller than the רבנן's.

steps.title: The משנה's measure for bran
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the שיעור for סובין is enough to put on the opening of a goldsmiths' crucible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bran: enough to put on the opening of the goldsmiths' crucible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, which is bran. It gives the amount that makes a person חייב for carrying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Goldsmiths placed bran on the opening of their crucible as part of their work. So the שיעור is the amount needed for that use, again matching a real job.

phrases.english: Bran: enough to put
on the opening of the crucible
of the goldsmiths.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוּבִּין כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן עַל פִּי כוּר שֶׁל צוֹרְפֵי זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying bran is חייב at the amount used on a goldsmiths' crucible opening.
